summary.text: Nikema Williams is the Democratic U.S. Representative for Georgia's 5th Congressional District and won re-election on November 3, 2026, according to unofficial results.

First elected in 2020 to succeed the late Rep. John Lewis, she previously worked in public policy and advocacy for Planned Parenthood Southeast and the National Domestic Workers Alliance, served in the Georgia State Senate, and chaired the Democratic Party of Georgia.

paragraphs.text: Williams was born in Columbus, Georgia, in 1978 and raised in Smiths Station, Alabama; she lives in Atlanta.
She graduated from Talladega College with a degree in biology, according to her official biography.
She moved to Atlanta in 2002 and joined the Young Democrats of Georgia, and was first vice chair of the Democratic Party of Georgia from 2011.

Before being elected to Congress she worked as vice president of Public Policy for Planned Parenthood Southeast, deputy director of civic engagement for the National Domestic Workers Alliance, and deputy executive director of Care in Action.
Williams won a 2017 special election to the Georgia State Senate and represented District 39 from 2017 to 2021.
She was elected chair of the Democratic Party of Georgia in January 2019, was re-elected in 2023, and stepped down in 2025.
After Rep. John Lewis died in July 2020, the Democratic Party of Georgia selected her to replace him on the November ballot; she won the November 3, 2020 general election with 85.1% of the vote.

On November 13, 2018, Georgia Department of Public Safety officers arrested Williams, then a state senator, with others protesting at the state Capitol over uncounted ballots in the governor's race; she said she was arrested for refusing to leave the floor of the building where she was a senator. The charges against her and the others were dismissed in June 2019.

In Congress, Williams serves on the House Financial Services Committee and, per her official biography, is Whip of the Democratic Women's Caucus and a member of the Congressional Black Caucus, Progressive Caucus, and New Democrat Coalition.
She won re-election in 2022 and 2024 (85.7% over John Salvesen in 2024) and the 2026 Democratic primary with 88.0% over Arnetress Beatty.
According to her official biography, she is married to Leslie Small and has a son.
She won the November 3, 2026 general election with 90.2% of the vote to John Salvesen's 9.8%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
